name: Signalizer: Lost Signal Finder
subtitle: Back to your last cell signal
promo: No signal? Signalizer brings you back to the last place you had service: your trail, a compass arrow, distance and walking time. 100% offline.
description:
You'll need it one day.

Signalizer remembers the last place your iPhone had cell service — and when the service drops, it brings you back to that last-signal point: your trail on a map that turns with you, a compass arrow, the exact distance and the walking time. An offline GPS compass that works with no internet and no network: in the desert, in the mountains, hiking, camping, anywhere with no signal.

100% offline. No internet. No account. No subscription. Total privacy — nothing ever leaves your iPhone.

LOST SIGNAL? WALK YOUR TRAIL BACK
• While you have service, Signalizer quietly saves your GPS location — offline, no internet.
• Always watch (optional): turn it on once and allow location "Always". The moment your iPhone loses service, your GPS trail starts recording by itself.
• Or tap "Heading out" before a desert trip or a hike. Signalizer keeps watching in the background while you use other apps or lock your phone. Tap "I'm back" when the network is back.
• No signal? Your trail is drawn on a map that turns with you, with the distance and walking time back to the last point with network — where you can call emergency services. Prefer the big compass arrow? Switch with one tap.
• One signal, one trail: each new signal loss starts one clear trail, never a confusing mess.

MARK YOUR PLACES
• "Mark this place" saves your car, your camp or a well. Later, a compass arrow with distance and walking time takes you back — offline, GPS only.
• Your places stay on your iPhone until you delete them.

AN EMERGENCY COMPASS FOR THE DESERT, THE MOUNTAINS AND THE OPEN ROAD
• Compass, bearing, distance and walking time from GPS only — offline, no network, no internet.
• Battery estimate: see roughly how many hours your battery will last while GPS is recording.
• Export your trail as a GPX file to share with rescuers or friends when you are back in coverage.
• Day mode readable in harsh desert sun, night mode for OLED screens, switching automatically at sunrise and sunset — computed from GPS, offline.
• The local emergency number for where you are, from GPS — offline.
• A short offline emergency guide: what to do when you're stranded in the desert or lost hiking with no signal, saving water and battery, distress signals for an emergency.
• Open the last-signal point or any marked place in Apple Maps or Google Maps.

NO INTERNET, 100% — TOTAL PRIVACY
Signalizer never connects to the internet, so it cannot send anything — real privacy, not promises. Location, trail and places are stored only on your iPhone and deleted when you delete the app. No ads, no tracking, no analytics, no account.

For everyone who heads into the desert, goes hiking or camping off-grid. One-time purchase. No subscription. No internet. Available in 46 languages.

FAQ
• Does it really work with no internet? Yes, 100% offline — Signalizer never uses the internet, and GPS works with no network.
• Does the compass need a network? No, the compass, distance and walking time come from GPS and the iPhone's sensors only.
• What happens in an emergency? Follow your trail or the compass arrow back to your last signal, then call emergency services as soon as the network is back.
• Does it keep watching if I close the app? Yes, if you just switch apps or lock the phone. If you swipe Signalizer away in the app switcher, iOS stops it — open it again before you head out.
• Privacy? Total privacy — offline, no account, no internet, and no data ever leaves your iPhone.
• Battery? Always watch uses GPS fully only after the signal is lost; "Heading out" uses GPS for one trip. The night mode saves battery too.
• Why no signal bars? iPhone doesn't let apps read signal strength, so Signalizer reacts when service is lost and when it comes back.
